transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… what brings me in is I feel like I’ve got this motor humming under my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like staff meetings at work, or even church event briefings—those can go on longer than you think—and I’m shifting around, standing up, finding some excuse to go check something or move chairs or whatever. I don’t mean to be disruptive, I just… sitting there feels almost impossible sometimes.
Did you have this same hard-to-sit-still feeling when you were a child?

Yeah, yeah, I did. I mean, I remember in grade school getting in trouble for popping up out of my seat all the time, or blurting stuff out over the teacher. And I’d start doing the worksheet or whatever before she’d even finished giving the directions.

My mom used to say I was “wound too tight,” which—funny, she said that about the old vacuum cleaner too when it made that whining noise, but with me she meant I just couldn’t settle. So, yeah, it was there when I was a kid.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or “up” for several days in a row?

Um… I’m not sure I’d call it “up” like that. Energized, maybe, but that’s sort of my normal, if that makes sense. I’m kind of always moving.

Several days in a row though… I don’t know. Like, when we’ve got a big cleanup at work after some event, I’ll be running around more than usual, and everybody’s asking where the mop heads are, and the floor buffer’s acting up—actually that machine is older than some of the guys using it—but I don’t think that’s what you mean.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed some special stretch of days where I felt unusually energized in a different way.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry some, sure. Everybody worries, right? Bills, whether I remembered to lock the supply closet, whether the floor’s still wet where someone might slip—actually those little yellow signs disappear all the time, I swear people use them like step stools or something.

But worrying about lots of different things all the time? I’m not sure I’d say that. I haven’t really thought of myself as a big worrier, more like I get caught up in whatever’s right in front of me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent pattern of hyperactivity/impulsivity beginning in childhood and continuing into adulthood, with difficulty remaining seated, excessive motor restlessness, blurting out answers, and acting before instructions are completed. Symptoms occur across settings (school, work, church) and cause functional problems. Interview responses do not support episodic mania or generalized anxiety as primary explanations.
